card.name: Past-tense verb right after a subject noun
card.fires_on: A verb in past or participle form placed directly after a subject noun, with no helper verb. It starts a main clause or a reduced clause, as in 'Lovastatin produced' or 'reactions characterized'.

modes.label: Participle after a condition
modes.description: A participle such as characterized follows a medical condition or reaction name and introduces its description.

modes.label: Past verb after a subject
modes.description: A past-tense verb such as produced, covered or packed follows a drug, group or crowd subject and begins the main action.

card.plain: It marks a verb in the past tense that comes straight after the thing it describes, like 'the drug produced'.
